l4_steps.name: Receive inbound contact via omnichannel
l4_steps.input: Customer call, webchat, email, or social media contact event
l4_steps.output: Contact session initiated; channel and intent captured
l4_steps.pain_point: Channel fragmentation — voice, chat, email, and social handled by separate queues, driving repeat contacts and inflated contact volume

l4_steps.name: Attempt IVR / AI chatbot self-service
l4_steps.input: Contact session, customer-stated intent, IVR menu selection
l4_steps.output: Self-service resolution or escalation flag to live agent queue
l4_steps.pain_point: IVR containment collapses during IRROP events; customers bypass bot with repeated keypress-zero, spiking live agent demand by up to 300%

l4_steps.name: Route contact to skilled agent queue
l4_steps.input: Identified customer intent, agent skill tags, real-time queue depth
l4_steps.output: Contact queued to appropriate agent team; estimated wait time published
l4_steps.kpi: Average Speed of Answer (ASA) ≤90 seconds; abandonment rate ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Skill-tag mismatches in WFM routing rules direct contacts to wrong specialisms (e.g. loyalty queries to general-service agents), increasing Average Handle Time by 20–35%

l4_steps.name: Authenticate customer identity
l4_steps.input: Customer-provided name, booking reference, FFP number, or date of birth
l4_steps.output: Identity verification flag set in CRM; authentication level recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Authentication success rate ≥98%; failed authentication escalation rate ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: PCI-DSS compliance prohibits agents from handling raw card data; non-FFP member identity verification has no single standard, causing inconsistent agent behaviour and potential fraud exposure

l4_steps.name: Retrieve PNR and loyalty profile from PSS
l4_steps.input: Booking reference or loyalty account number
l4_steps.output: PNR itinerary, fare basis, ticket number, and loyalty tier displayed on agent desktop
l4_steps.kpi: PNR retrieval response time ≤5 seconds; PSS availability ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Codeshare or interline itineraries may not surface fully in Altéa; agent must switch to a partner portal or call partner CLC, adding 3–5 minutes per contact

l4_steps.name: Create or update CRM case record
l4_steps.input: Contact reason, PNR details, loyalty profile, channel identifier
l4_steps.output: Case ID created with linked PNR, reason code, channel tag, and priority flag
l4_steps.kpi: Mandatory field completion rate ≥99%; case creation accuracy ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent reason-code taxonomy in Salesforce yields corrupted trend reporting; root-cause signals for systemic issues (e.g. baggage carousel failures) go undetected for hours

l4_steps.name: Categorise and diagnose customer issue
l4_steps.input: Customer statement, PNR details, case record, NOC disruption feed
l4_steps.output: Issue category assigned (delay, refund, baggage, loyalty, complaint, IRROP)
l4_steps.pain_point: IRROP-related contact spikes arrive before NOC disruption alerts propagate to Salesforce; agents categorise manually without system-side context, slowing diagnosis

l4_steps.name: Apply Tier 1 resolution per service policy
l4_steps.input: Issue category, fare rules from ATPCO, service policy matrix, customer loyalty tier
l4_steps.output: Resolution action determined: rebooking, waiver, information provision, or compensation
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents must toggle between Altéa and Salesforce with no unified desktop; dual-screen context switching increases AHT by 15–20% and introduces data-entry errors

l4_steps.name: Rebook or modify flight in PSS
l4_steps.input: Customer rebooking preference, available seat inventory, fare rules
l4_steps.output: Revised PNR confirmed; itinerary change notification sent to customer
l4_steps.kpi: Rebooking completion rate ≥95%; change-fee waiver audit compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Involuntary rebooking fare-difference calculations require manual ATPCO fare rule lookup — no automated waiver logic in Altéa — leading to over- or under-collection and regulatory exposure

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved case to Tier 2 specialist
l4_steps.input: Unresolved case ID, escalation reason code, full interaction transcript
l4_steps.output: Case warm-transferred with context; Tier 2 specialist assigned and notified
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation rate ≤15%; Tier 2 resolution within 24 hours ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Case context is frequently lost during warm transfers; Tier 2 agents ask customers to repeat information, reducing CSAT by an average of 0.4 points per repeat

l4_steps.name: Assess service recovery compensation eligibility
l4_steps.input: Disruption type and cause, fare class, loyalty tier, EC261/DOT regulation applicability flags
l4_steps.output: Compensation eligibility decision (Y/N); recommended recovery action documented in case
l4_steps.kpi: Compensation decision accuracy ≥98%; EC261 regulatory compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: EC261 applicability for EU-origin flights requires manual legal review — no automated rule engine in Salesforce; agents under volume pressure make incorrect eligibility decisions, creating regulatory liability

l4_steps.name: Issue compensation — miles, voucher, or refund
l4_steps.input: Compensation decision, customer loyalty account, fare paid, voucher policy matrix
l4_steps.output: Miles credited to FFP account, travel voucher issued, or refund initiated in PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Miles crediting accuracy 100%; voucher issuance within 24 hours; DOT-mandated cash refund within 7 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Miles issuance, voucher generation, and PSS refund initiation are in three separate systems with no unified API; dual-entry requirement creates a 2–3% error rate on high-volume disruption days

l4_steps.name: Process policy exception with supervisor approval
l4_steps.input: Agent exception request, case notes, customer loyalty tier and lifetime value
l4_steps.output: Exception approved or denied; case notes updated with justification and supervisor ID
l4_steps.kpi: Exception approval turnaround ≤10 minutes; monthly exception rate tracked as % of total contacts
l4_steps.pain_point: Supervisor approval queue backs up during IRROP events; customers placed on hold >5 minutes, reducing Customer Effort Score (CES) and increasing call abandonment

l4_steps.name: Confirm resolution and close case
l4_steps.input: Resolution actions completed, customer verbal or written confirmation
l4_steps.output: Case status set to Resolved; wrap-up code, resolution notes, and handle time recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Same-day case closure rate ≥85%; after-call work (ACW) time ≤90 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents under volume pressure skip ACW documentation; incomplete case notes degrade QA coaching effectiveness and root-cause trending by up to 30%

l4_steps.name: Trigger post-contact NPS / CSAT survey
l4_steps.input: Case closed event, customer email or SMS on file, marketing opt-in status
l4_steps.output: CSAT / NPS survey dispatched via email or SMS; response tracked in Medallia dashboard
l4_steps.pain_point: Survey fatigue among frequent flyers who receive multiple survey requests per journey leg; opt-out rate rising 3–5% per quarter, eroding feedback sample size

l4_steps.name: QA review, score, and coach agent
l4_steps.input: Recorded interactions, case notes, CSAT scores, compliance checklist
l4_steps.output: QA scorecard per interaction; coaching flags raised; compliance audit trail maintained
l4_steps.kpi: QA sample rate ≥10% of all contacts; QA score ≥85%; coaching session within 5 business days of flag
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual QA sampling misses systemic issues; AI-assisted speech analytics available in NICE CXone but not fully deployed across all contact types, leaving compliance blind spots
